literature_notes: The sole ledger entry, L1, describes a CaM tag fused to 'the extracellular domain of mIL-12Rβ2 (D1-D6)' co-expressed with mIL-12Rβ1-DAPK1 for formation of a purifiable receptor complex for structural/biochemical characterisation. Two independent disqualifications apply. First, the D1-D6 notation in the quote denotes the six fibronectin-type-III ectodomain modules of IL-12Rβ2; the construct is used alongside a DAPK1 dimerisation-domain fusion and a CaM purification handle specifically to produce a soluble, purifiable complex for structural studies — it is a soluble ectodomain, not a full-length membrane-anchored receptor, and therefore falls under the explicit exclusion ('a soluble ECTODOMAIN or single-domain construct secreted as a separate protein for structure, binding or crystallography'). Second, even if the construct were accepted as full-length, the quote states no residue number for the CaM insertion; the tag position is entirely unstated, so insert_after_residue cannot be pinned. A topology-derived N-terminal placement (after signal-peptide cleavage at residue 23, giving insert_after_residue = 23, residue_before = A, residue_after = K) would require confirmed evidence of a full-length membrane-anchored construct, which the quote does not provide. The construct is also mouse IL-12Rβ2, not human, though this alone would not disqualify it. Because both primary disqualifications hold independently, L1 does not ground any surface tag site, and the correct answer is zero sites.
